post_text:
10 days. 10 government datasets. 10 findings.
Every number in this report came from a website you can open right now.
Not one required a subscription, a FOIA request, or a university login.

The data was always there.

Here's what ten days of systematic public data analysis found: the crisis in American public education is not uniform — it's predictable. Mississippi reads better than New York on an income-adjusted basis because they made a curriculum decision in 2013. Cleveland cut absenteeism from 22% to 18% while Memphis went from 20% to 29.6% — same poverty rate, different intervention model. Utah gets 3.6× more reading proficiency per dollar than New York.

The patterns were in plain sight in free government spreadsheets. They just needed someone to look.

→ Full 10-finding research report — one sourced finding per day, all linked to live dashboards
→ All 10 interactive dashboards — live on GitHub Pages, all code public
→ Methodology section — 4 design principles applied across every day of analysis

Day 10 of 10 — Challenge complete. From Memphis to 50 States.
